item_verdicts.call_sites: no production symbol or call site; the measure is reckon.doccheck.audit_fragment_ids and audit_composed_record_ids over the plan's fragment directory and composed record.
item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base 07ad28145; 28751a7ee changes only id attribute values across 37 fragments (masking id values makes base and head byte-identical), 4c6c2b253 adds only the 24-line landing fragment, all inside the declared scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: the repair node's measure is that the plan's composed record audits clean and every renamed id begins with its file's node id. Both hold: audit_fragment_ids reads 18 at base and 0 at head; composed-record audit drops from 19 to the one header-duplicate warn present at base; all 90 new ids are stem-prefixed; no non-colliding id or prose changed; no link in docs/ targets a renamed id of this plan.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is a node-prefixed rename of every colliding element id in the crew-runtime-positive-controls fragments; commit 28751a7ee applies exactly that and my independent parse finds all 90 renamed occurrences prefixed with the file stem, 18 distinct ids, matching the base collisions both directions.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the rename commit 28751a7ee and the landing commit 4c6c2b253, the gate command (gate_fragment_ids.py, audit_fragment_ids + structural/link checks), the base/head arms 18 findings EXIT=1 / 0 findings EXIT=0, and the per-id occurrence counts; the landing line's composed-record 19->1 reconciles with the full audit_file result.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares the 37 renamed fragments plus the crew-observability-truth landing fragment plus a figures directory; both commits change only files inside that set.

justifications.durability: the repair is a data change with no test file in the write scope, so it adds no regression test of its own; the guard that keeps future fragments clean is the existing duplicate-element-id audit (audit_fragment_ids / the scoped composed-record check this section's sibling node added), which the run's own gate exercises and which now reads 0 for this plan's directory — the rename itself is not self-guarding beyond that audit.
justifications.evidence: the manifest's gate logs are reproducible and I reproduced them independently: extracting the fragment directory at base 07ad28145 and head 4c6c2b253 and running reckon.doccheck.audit_fragment_ids gives 18 findings at base and 0 at head; audit_composed_record_ids on the composed record gives 18 at base and 0 at head; the full doccheck.audit_file on the composed record gives 19 findings at base and 1 at head, the survivor being the header-duplicate warn present at base too, which reconciles the manifest's stated 19->1 composed-record figure with the run's own logs (fragment-ids-base.log EXIT=1, fragment-ids-head.log EXIT=0).
justifications.fit: the prefix is the fragment file's stem, which is the node id composition keys the fragments on, so sibling fragments composed into one record carry distinct anchors; the landing fragment deliberately carries no element ids (verified 0 id= and no figure) and so adds no collision to the record it is checked by; the two docs/ hrefs to a bare 'measure' resolve into other plans' landed records (artifact-feeds-and-reader, dependency-edge-semantics) and none targets a renamed id of this plan (grep finds no link to crew-runtime-positive-controls-landed#<renamed id>).
justifications.goal_fidelity: the node goal is to rename every colliding element id in the crew-runtime-positive-controls fragments so each begins with its fragment's node id; commit 28751a7ee renames 90 occurrences of 18 distinct bare ids across 37 files, and my independent parse of the base->head diff confirms all 90 new ids begin with the file stem plus '-', the 18 distinct old ids exactly equal the 18 duplicate-element-id ids audit_fragment_ids finds at base 07ad28145 (0 mismatches in either direction), and no bare renamed id survives in the head fragments.
justifications.scope_discipline: both commits change only files inside the manifest's declared write scope: git diff --name-only 07ad28145..4c6c2b253 lists the 37 renamed fragments plus the landing fragment, all 38 within the 39-path scope (the one unused entry is the figures directory, which the landing fragment does not populate); masking every id="..." value makes base and head byte-identical across all 37 fragment files (0 files with any non-id change), so no prose, attribute or non-colliding id moved, and no plan file was touched; both commit messages carry a body with no plan identifier and no AI attribution.
